bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Confident and strategic; focused on long-term infrastructure transformation; clear emphasis on Kavach and data centers as growth engines; transparent on subcontracting and revenue recognition
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: RailTel is effectively acting as a prime integrator for Kavach — owning full revenue recognition while subcontracting 30-40% of execution (cabling, towers) — creating high-margin, high-revenue project control without capex burden on field work
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Pan-India neutral optic fibre network of over 63,000 route kilometres laid on railway right of way, plus 21,000+ km of city access network — a footprint that is very difficult to replicate
- Navratna CPSE status under the Ministry of Railways, which management states confers enhanced operational and financial independence and strengthens positioning with government, defence and other trusted-source-preferring buyers
- Only telecom PSU that is 100% debt free and a consistently profit-making and dividend-paying PSU in the telecom sector
- Long-standing strategic relationship with Indian Railways as an incumbent implementer of mission-critical connectivity, surveillance, e-Office, Wi-Fi and signalling projects
- Track record of selection for national mission-mode programmes including the National Knowledge Network, BharatNet Phase I and USOF-funded optical fibre connectivity in North East India
- Certification stack (CMMI Maturity Level-5, multiple ISO standards) and Tier-III certified Data Centres, RailCloud, SOC and NOC underpinning service reliability
- End-to-end integration capability spanning telecom, railway signalling, Data Centre, cloud and cybersecurity, enabling integrated bundled offerings
- Robust order book exceeding ₹10,400 crore as on date, with fresh work orders of ₹7,363 crore secured during FY 2025-26
- Diversified customer base beyond Railways across Defence, Healthcare, Banking, Mining, Smart Cities, Insurance and Government projects
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Sectoral concentration on Government and railway projects — Dependence on Government and railway-sector projects exposes the Company to sectoral policy shifts, public expenditure cycles and infrastructure-prioritisation trends. Mitigation is diversification across State Governments, BFSI, healthcare, education, defence and enterprise customers, along with expansion of telecom and managed-service offerings.
- Project execution risk on complex multi-state contracts — Complex multi-state ICT, telecom, railway modernisation and Data Centre projects carry risks of delay due to field conditions, scope changes, cost escalation, dependency on external agencies and contractual execution challenges — directly relevant given that project business accounts for the majority of turnover. Managed through a strengthened project monitoring framework, milestone-based execution review and disciplined change management.
- Competitive intensity from private telecom operators and hyperscale cloud providers — Market risk that competitive intensity and evolving market dynamics may impact growth opportunities and margins; countered by customer diversification, differentiated positioning as a trusted Government and PSU digital infrastructure provider, value-added managed services and integrated offerings.
- Technology obsolescence — Rapid evolution and obsolescence of telecom, AI, cloud and cybersecurity technologies may impact the competitiveness of legacy infrastructure and service platforms, requiring continuous technology refresh, OEM partnerships, phased modernisation and sustained investment in next-generation digital infrastructure.
- Cyber security risk across networks, Data Centres and customer workloads — Increasing sophistication of cyber threats targeting telecom networks, Data Centres, enterprise systems and customer workloads may lead to service disruption, data compromise and regulatory exposure. Mitigated by a multi-layered cybersecurity architecture, a Security Operations Centre, periodic VAPT and audits, and incident-response mechanisms.
- People risk — attracting and retaining emerging-technology talent — Attracting, developing and retaining skilled manpower in emerging technology domains remains a challenge amid increasing industry competition for talent, specifically in cybersecurity, cloud, AI and Data Centre operations; addressed through skilling and certification programmes, leadership development, institutional collaborations, succession planning and DPE-aligned compensation.
- Contractor / vendor dependence — Dependence on contractors, OEMs and vendors for execution, supplies and support services may impact timelines, quality and operational continuity; managed through vendor due diligence, a multi-vendor strategy, contractual safeguards and diversification of supply sources.
- Information and data-protection risk — Increased digitalisation and evolving data-protection obligations elevate risks relating to confidentiality, integrity, availability and governance of information assets, requiring information-security controls, a data-governance framework, periodic compliance reviews and DPDP-related readiness measures.
- Strategy risk from shifting digital-infrastructure trends — Rapid technological evolution, changing customer expectations and emerging digital infrastructure trends could affect long-term strategic positioning and business sustainability; mitigated by continuous strategic review, diversification into Data Centre, cloud, cybersecurity and emerging digital services, and partnership-led growth.
- Sustainability / ESG expectation risk — Increasing ESG expectations, climate-related disclosures and sustainability requirements may impact operations, infrastructure planning and stakeholder perception; addressed through BRSR-aligned disclosures, a sustainability governance framework and energy-efficiency initiatives.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body: RailTel was incorporated in September 2000 with the twin mandate of modernising the telecom system for train control, operations and safety across Indian Railways, and of creating a nationwide broadband, telecom and multimedia network using right of way along railway tracks. Today it operates an optic fibre network of over 63,000 route kilometres covering 7,000+ railway stations, with over 21,000 km of citywide access network, and delivers Telecom, IT & ICT services, railway signalling, Data Centres, cloud and digital solutions. Its customers include Indian Railways, government organisations and ministries, educational institutions, corporates, banks and NBFCs, private enterprises and retail broadband subscribers.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Telecom Services:** National Long Distance (NLD) services, Internet Service Provider (ISP) services, Infrastructure Provider (IP-1) services / telecom infrastructure maintenance, RailWire home broadband (partner-led model), IPTV and bundled high-speed internet / OTT plans, Enterprise connectivity and OFC backbone / high-capacity backhaul
- **Project Business (ICT & railway projects):** IP-based Video Surveillance Systems at railway stations, Hospital Management Information System (HMIS) for railway hospitals, NIC e-Office deployment for Indian Railways and other organisations, Free high-speed Wi-Fi at railway stations, Kavach (indigenous Automatic Train Protection) implementation, Tunnel Communication Systems, Electronic Interlocking and Automatic Block Signalling, AI-based Smart Enforcement System (Transport Department, Government of Karnataka)
- **Data Centre, Cloud & Security:** Tier-III (Design & Facility) certified Data Centres, RailCloud platform, Edge Data Centres in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, Data Centre colocation / managed services, Security Operation Centre (SOC) and Network Operation Centres (NOC)
- **International / MEA-funded:** Electronic LED Scoreboard, Sabina Park Stadium, Kingston, Jamaica, Supply of 2,000 Make-in-India laptops for school students in Trinidad & Tobago, BHISHM Cube AI-enabled portable modular healthcare system (supply and marketing for Aarogya Maitri Cell, Government of India)

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Horizon 1 (FY 2026-27) — Consolidate: operationalise existing Data Centre capacity expansion and initial edge deployments; execute committed railway modernisation milestones including KAVACH and station projects; achieve baseline DPDP and telecom cyber-security compliance maturity; strengthen the managed-services revenue mix and tail revenue from completed projects.
- Horizon 2 (FY 2027-29) — Expand: scale the Data Centre and edge footprint in alignment with sovereign hosting demand; mature cybersecurity-as-a-service and managed-cloud propositions; deepen AI-enabled operations and customer solutions in selected verticals; expand engagement with State Governments, BFSI and defence.
- Horizon 3 (FY 2029-31) — Lead: position as a leading domestic sovereign-cloud and edge-infrastructure operator; establish a credible international ICT presence in selected geographies; embed AI-readiness across the network, Data Centre estate and customer-facing solutions; continue to anchor Indian Railways' digital transformation as the lead ICT integration partner.
- Diversify away from a purely railway/telecom base into Data Centre, cloud, cybersecurity and emerging digital services through selective investments, partnership-led growth and periodic business portfolio assessment (stated as mitigation of Strategy Risk).
- Diversify the customer mix across State Governments, BFSI, healthcare, education, defence and enterprise customers, along with expansion of telecom and managed-service offerings, to reduce dependence on Government and railway-sector projects.
- Position integrated bundled offerings for the Indian Railways customer by tightening the strategic linkage between railway ICT, Data Centre capability and cybersecurity.
- Differentiate as a trusted Government and PSU digital infrastructure provider with value-added managed services against private telecom operators and hyperscale cloud providers.
- Treat human capital as a strategic asset: structured upskilling in Data Centre operations, cybersecurity, cloud-native engineering, AI and data engineering, KAVACH and railway signalling; sponsored industry certifications; institutional partnerships with IITs, IIITs, IIMs and NITIE; and structured succession planning across Functional Directors, Executive Directors and Group General Managers.
- Use Navratna status to engage more flexibly with external talent for specialised emerging-technology roles and to pursue strategic investments and partnerships.
- Continuous technology refresh through OEM partnerships, phased infrastructure modernisation and focused investment in next-generation digital infrastructure.
- RailTel states it is focused on enhancing shareholder value and has a consistent track record of dividend payment. Dividends are declared in line with its Dividend Distribution Policy, framed under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations and the DIPAM guidelines on "Capital Restructuring of Central Public Enterprises", and the policy is published on the Company's website. For FY 2025-26 the Board declared and paid interim dividend twice, totalling ₹2 per share, and has recommended a final dividend of ₹1.25 per share subject to shareholder approval, taking the total for the year to 32.50% of paid-up share capital. No amount was transferred to the General Reserves during the year; profit earned was appropriated. The Company describes itself as the only telecom PSU that is 100% debt free and a consistently profit-making and dividend-paying PSU in the telecom sector, and it also pays a 7% revenue share on services to Indian Railways and an 8% licence fee to DoT. Reinvestment intent is capex-led: planned capital expenditure of approximately ₹241 crore in FY 2026-27 towards network expansion, data centre infrastructure and technology upgradation, with Navratna status cited as giving enhanced operational and financial independence to pursue strategic investments and partnerships. Governance note relevant to capital stewardship: as on the date of the report the Board comprised seven directors with a vacancy of five Independent Directors, for which an appointment request has been made to the Ministry of Railways; the Chairperson is an Executive Director, so half the Board should comprise Independent Directors under Regulation 17.
- ESG framework anchored on the SEBI-mandated BRSR disclosure regime, the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct (NGRBC), and India's national priorities on clean-energy transition, digital inclusion and responsible governance.
- Climate change identified in the BRSR materiality table as an opportunity (positive financial implication): demand for energy-efficient digital networks, green infrastructure and low-carbon technology solutions, with improving operational efficiency expected to reduce carbon footprint and greenhouse emissions.
- Sustainable supply chain management identified as a material opportunity, given procurement of telecom equipment, IT infrastructure, network components and project-related services, for operational efficiency, regulatory compliance and supplier accountability.
- E-waste management identified as a material opportunity, given extensive use of telecom equipment, IT systems, electronic devices and network infrastructure.
- Health, safety and well-being of employees identified as a material opportunity and a key organisational priority.
- Diversity and inclusion identified as a material opportunity for building a progressive, equitable and collaborative workplace across diverse geographical locations and functional domains.
- Customer privacy and cybersecurity identified as a material opportunity, with strong cybersecurity systems and data protection required across telecom, cloud, data centre and ICT services.
- ISO 14001:2015 certification for Environmental Management System, alongside ISO 27001:2022, ISO 27017:2015 and ISO 27018:2019 covering information security and cloud data privacy.
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers (RailWire subscriber ticketing portal) and value-chain partners (CPGRAM, Independent External Monitors and a published Integrity Pact).
- Permanent-employee turnover rate of 3.91% in FY 2025-26 (4.24% male, 1.49% female), improved from 6.36% in FY 2024-25; no employees fall under the worker category.
- Women represent 12.50% of the Board of Directors and 11.93% of permanent employees; the differently-abled permanent employee cohort is 90.91% male and 9.09% female.
- BRSR reporting boundary is standalone, covering the organisational boundary where the Company has operational control; no external assurance provider has been appointed for the BRSR.
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: RailTel's expansion is footprint- and platform-led rather than plant-led. Capital expenditure of approximately ₹272 crore was incurred during FY 2025-26, mainly on OFC-related assets, Data Centre and Telecom & Radio equipment, and the Chairman states that a capital expenditure of approximately ₹241 crore is planned during FY 2026-27 towards network expansion, data centre infrastructure and technology upgradation. The largest single build is the upcoming 10 MW Data Centre at Noida, where work is progressing as planned and the first phase of 5 MW capacity is expected to become operational shortly; alongside it, RailTel is developing Edge Data Centres particularly across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities to support low-latency digital services, with two Edge Data Centres already completed and work on additional sites progressing. These facilities are positioned to serve Artificial Intelligence, healthcare, cloud, content delivery and IoT workloads, and RailTel has entered partnerships with a number of organisations for Data Centre colocation and managed-service offerings. On the network side, the existing estate spans over 63,000 route kilometres of optic fibre covering 7,000+ railway stations plus over 21,000 km of citywide access network, with the Company describing capacity augmentation in its core network as it pushes into the enterprise segment. Project-side expansion is anchored on railway modernisation: multiple Kavach (Automatic Train Protection) projects in East Central Railway and West Central Railway covering more than 2,000 route kilometres, Tunnel Communication Systems on the Dharam-Banihal section in Jammu & Kashmir, the Rishikesh-Karnaprayag section, the Sivok-Rangpo New BG Rail Line project and the Bhairabi-Sairang New Single line Section of Lumding Division, plus several Electronic Interlocking projects. Digital-service rollouts continued at scale, including IP-based Video Surveillance Systems at more than 5,000 railway stations, HMIS across 709 railway hospitals, NIC e-Office for 150+ organisations beyond Indian Railways with roughly 45 more in progress, and free high-speed Wi-Fi maintained and expanded at over 6,117 railway stations.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects the macroeconomic environment described by the RBI and the Economic Survey to remain supportive over FY 2026-27 and the medium term, with sustained domestic demand, benign inflation, consistent Government capital expenditure and reform momentum translating into a stable demand environment for the Company's core service lines.
- The progressive recognition of digital infrastructure as core economic infrastructure is described as a structural elevation the Company expects to benefit from over multiple budget cycles.
- The telecom sector's transition from network deployment to monetisation, sustained Government commitment to rural connectivity through BharatNet and the National Broadband Mission, and modernisation of the spectrum framework collectively support sustained demand for the Company's OFC backbone, NLD and enterprise connectivity offerings.
- The structural shift towards sovereign hosting, the maturing cloud and managed-services model and the deepening cybersecurity compliance landscape are expected to drive sustained demand for the Company's Data Centre, cloud and security offerings.
- Edge Data Centres are expected to emerge as a meaningful incremental opportunity over the medium term, leveraging the Company's distinctive distributed footprint.
- The Company's AI positioning, anchored on the application-led national framework, is expected to mature progressively over the next two to three years.
- Railway digital modernisation — particularly KAVACH and adjacent ICT programmes — is described as providing multi-year demand visibility that is unusual in scale and clarity, and as a multi-year anchor for the business.
- The Company's long-standing role as a CPSE implementing partner for national connectivity programmes is expected to position it to participate in upcoming phases and adjacent service opportunities.
- Management explicitly caveats that the Company does not project specific numerical financial outcomes in the outlook section, and that all sectoral and macroeconomic projections reproduce Indian Government projections without independent revision.
- Beyond KAVACH, the railway modernisation programme encompassing tunnel communication systems, station redevelopment with integrated ICT and Video Surveillance, signalling modernisation, and passenger information and announcement systems is described as collectively constituting a multi-year, mission-critical opportunity pool for the Company, anchored on its long-standing partnership with Indian Railways.
- Addressable pipeline context (Indian Railways' own plan, not the Company's order book): Indian Railways plans to expand the KAVACH network by 9,000 route kilometres over the next two years and thereafter expects growth of up to 10,000 route kilometres per year; trackside installations are underway on 7,100 route kilometres.
- Management states its integration expertise, partnership ecosystem and technical certifications place it in a strong position to participate meaningfully in the railway modernisation programme over FY 2026-27 and beyond.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

promoters.name: President of India, acting through the Ministry of Railways (MoR), Government of India
promoters.role: Government promoter of this "Government Company" under Section 2(45) of the Companies Act, 2013, holding 72.84% of the total paid-up equity share capital; under the Articles of Association the power to appoint/nominate all Directors on the Board vests with the President of India acting through MoR. RailTel is a Navratna CPSE under the administrative control of the Ministry of Railways.

risks.note: Dependence on Government and railway-sector projects exposes the Company to sectoral policy shifts, public expenditure cycles and infrastructure-prioritisation trends. Mitigation is diversification across State Governments, BFSI, healthcare, education, defence and enterprise customers, along with expansion of telecom and managed-service offerings.
risks.risk: Sectoral concentration on Government and railway projects

risks.note: Complex multi-state ICT, telecom, railway modernisation and Data Centre projects carry risks of delay due to field conditions, scope changes, cost escalation, dependency on external agencies and contractual execution challenges — directly relevant given that project business accounts for the majority of turnover. Managed through a strengthened project monitoring framework, milestone-based execution review and disciplined change management.
risks.risk: Project execution risk on complex multi-state contracts

risks.note: Market risk that competitive intensity and evolving market dynamics may impact growth opportunities and margins; countered by customer diversification, differentiated positioning as a trusted Government and PSU digital infrastructure provider, value-added managed services and integrated offerings.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity from private telecom operators and hyperscale cloud providers

risks.note: Rapid evolution and obsolescence of telecom, AI, cloud and cybersecurity technologies may impact the competitiveness of legacy infrastructure and service platforms, requiring continuous technology refresh, OEM partnerships, phased modernisation and sustained investment in next-generation digital infrastructure.

Increasing sophistication of cyber threats targeting telecom networks, Data Centres, enterprise systems and customer workloads may lead to service disruption, data compromise and regulatory exposure. Mitigated by a multi-layered cybersecurity architecture, a Security Operations Centre, periodic VAPT and audits, and incident-response mechanisms.
risks.risk: Cyber security risk across networks, Data Centres and customer workloads

risks.note: Attracting, developing and retaining skilled manpower in emerging technology domains remains a challenge amid increasing industry competition for talent, specifically in cybersecurity, cloud, AI and Data Centre operations; addressed through skilling and certification programmes, leadership development, institutional collaborations, succession planning and DPE-aligned compensation.
risks.risk: People risk — attracting and retaining emerging-technology talent

risks.note: Dependence on contractors, OEMs and vendors for execution, supplies and support services may impact timelines, quality and operational continuity; managed through vendor due diligence, a multi-vendor strategy, contractual safeguards and diversification of supply sources.

Increased digitalisation and evolving data-protection obligations elevate risks relating to confidentiality, integrity, availability and governance of information assets, requiring information-security controls, a data-governance framework, periodic compliance reviews and DPDP-related readiness measures.

meta.thesis: RailTel delivered strong Q1FY26 growth (33% revenue YoY) driven by railway project wins and data center expansion, with Kavach orders now forming a critical long-term revenue pillar; the company is transitioning from a passive telecom provider to an integrated railway digital infrastructure player.
